Apple Icon Composer

Apple’s 2025 tool for building layered app icons from Liquid Glass, with controls for specular light, blur, translucency, and shadow.

Source
Apple Newsroom, June 9, 2025
Creator
Apple
Made
2025 (announced June 9, 2025)
Style
Liquid Glass (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Luminous, precise, dimensional
Evidence
Inspected the Apple Newsroom image Apple-WWDC25-Liquid-Glass-Icon-Composer-250609 (1960 × 1102, large_2x variant) in a scratchpad copy. A press render. Not stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Apple: Icon Composer annotates “layers for multiple rendering modes, with advanced features that include blurring, adjusting translucency, testing specular highlights, and previewing icons in various tints”. Apple Newsroom.

Apple: “the Dock, app icons, and widgets have all been crafted from multiple layers of Liquid Glass … with specular highlights”. Apple Newsroom.

Observed

  • A Mac window with three parts over a blue wave wallpaper: a layer list on the left, a large preview of the Podcasts icon in the middle, and an inspector on the right.
  • The icon is built from stacked translucent layers: a blue rounded square, two pale rings, and a white figure. Each layer has a lit rim, and the rings show the blue square through them.
  • The inspector has a “Liquid Glass” group with Mode (Individual), Specular (on), Blur 21.8 %, Translucency 50 %, Dark 42 %, and Shadow (Neutral, 50 %).
  • The toolbar is a row of separate capsules: appearance toggle, grid, light angle (34°), and zoom (50 %). Small previews at the bottom show the icon in default, dark, and mono looks.
  • The sidebar and inspector are light, translucent panels inset in the window with rounded corners.

Why it belongs

The tool turns the material into a short list of parameters with a single light direction. This is close to how a CSS version must work: a fill, a blur, a highlight angle, and a shadow.

Borrow

Fix one light angle for the whole interface, and place every specular highlight on the edge that faces it.

See also the 2025 and 2026 icon edge.
